Issued at 335 AM EDT Thu Oct 15 2026

=====Foggy, With Spotty Showers and Storms This Afternoon=====

A game of cat and mouse is ongoing between departing clouds to the 
east, and approaching low to mid level clouds from the west. In 
areas that have seen a few hours of clearing, dense fog is forming. 
Timing and forecasting how thick the fog settles in is tricky 
because fog is hard to form with any cloud cover. Be that as it may. 
a Dense Fog Advisory will likely be issued very shortly to account 
for the observed dense fog in some areas that aren't in the typical 
valley locations, favored in areas from near Bowling Green towards 
Lexington and places NW from there, including the Louisville Metro. 
Though fog may not be quite as prevalent as a few nights ago, it 
will nonetheless cause concern for drivers in the morning.

Beyond fog, winds are light as a cold front has nearly bisected our 
CWA. Nearly calm winds are present across the CWA, with generally 
southerly flow south of an east-to-west line from just north of Lake 
Cumberland to just north of BWG. Spotty showers are beginning to 
bubble up and move into our western CWA as well. Spotty showers 
can't be ruled out for the rest of the morning. This signifies the 
return to SW flow later this morning and afternoon as a warm front 
lifts through the Ohio Valley today. Warm minimum temperature 
records may be broken later this morning considering how saturated 
we are (I'd imagine the whole CWA only has the chance to cool by 
another degree or two).

Eventually, as the warm front lifts through our area, it will slowly 
raise cloud ceilings, scour out fog, and generally push lower PoPs 
to our north. SW flow may be enhanced due to the close presence of a 
developing low moving towards the Great Lakes region. When the warm 
front associated with this low passes to the north, there may be 
enough instability for storms to fire as it passes sometime after 12 
Noon EDT. For now, since moisture is so high, at least in the lower 
levels, clouds will be rather slow to clear for pure sunshine before 
storms fire. In between clouds though, enough instability could 
present strong to severe wind gusts. The best wind shear will avoid 
us to the NW, and as a result, the tornado threat will likely 
completely miss our area. Highs with this enhanced SW flow behind 
the front will be quick to warm though despite the morning cloud 
cover. There is still a question of how much cloud cover will stick 
around this afternoon but for now, high temperatures should be 
warmest in the south (south of I-64) in the mid to upper 80s. North 
of the interstate, clouds and rain will take the longest to clear 
with highs in the lower 80s to upper 70s. 

It should be said that despite the chance for severe weather, 
rainfall coverage will be scattered at best and move fairly 
progressively with the strong SW flow. Additional rainfall totals 
have a 75% of remaining under 0.5", with an extremely isolated risk 
of up to 2" of rain should a heavy downpour or two track over the 
same areas this afternoon. We are not expecting any flash flooding 
concerns today as the best severe risk and flooding risk remain too 
far north.

=====Strong Incoming Cold Front and Seasonable Warmth Next Week=====

SW flow will intensify as the impending cold behind the departing 
Great Lakes low gets closer and sweeps through early Friday morning. 
Winds will increase by early morning and grow stronger throughout 
the day. Temperatures will fall into the 60s for highs and cooling 
throughout the afternoon after frontal passage with wind gusts of 25-
35 MPH. 

Saturday, lows are chilly in the morning as temperatures really 
struggle to reach the upper 50s. There is increasing confidence in 
widespread frost Saturday night with clear skies and lows forecast 
in the mid to low 30s. We will likely issue products related to 
this when the time comes. 

Beyond Saturday, high temperatures very very slowly moderate as 
highs Sunday reach the mid 60s. Isolated frost may be possible, 
although the positioning of a high pressure may allow weak southerly 
flow to moderate us just enough to stay out of frost territory. Long 
range trend is dry, really through the rest of the week. 
Temperatures look to remain near normal eventually settling into the 
low 70s by midweek next week.
